class: TWO DIRECTIONS, and the patches run BOTH WAYS on purpose. (1) CORRUPTED -- Corpus Corporum broke a word Migne set correctly; repaired. (2) NORMALIZED -- Corpus Corporum silently tidied Migne's OWN defective type, or moved it toward the Clementine; REVERTED to what Migne printed, so the defect is visible and can take an honest [sic:] or [var:]. Reverting is not patching away a plate defect (which CLAUDE.md forbids) -- it is undoing the digitization's departure from the plate, which is exactly what this file is for. || RATE: ~2 sites per page, against a standing corpus estimate of THREE INSTANCES IN TOTAL for this class (brief Test 4). The rate, not the class, is the finding. || THREE of the corrupted sites (Dominius, Juant, infirmi ates) would each have drawn a false [sic:] -- a public accusation against Migne for the digitization's error.

The translator reached for corpus-as-control and found 'resistis' at 0792A, but that is a different person of the verb in a different sentence and could never have settled this. || CORRECTED 2026-08-28: the find/replace string originally written here ('qui superbis resistis, quia non est mundatus') does not occur at 0790B at all -- it is the DIFFERENT sentence at 0792A, and the patch therefore fired at the wrong column: it left 0790B's 'resisti' untouched and silently changed 0792A's plate-attested 'resistis' (2nd person, which the English at 0792A renders 'who resistest the proud') into 'resistit'. Find/replace re-aimed at the intended 0790B site; src/latin/9003/0016.md corrected by hand at both places. || RE-AIMED AGAIN 2026-08-28 (session lead): the corrected find still matched ZERO times, because the TEI sets a LINE BREAK between 'superbis' and 'resisti'. A zero-match patch makes chunk-work.mjs exit 1, and the hand-repair made to src/latin/9003/0016.md would have been erased by the next re-chunk with nothing to replace it. Find string now carries the newline and is verified to match once, at 0790B.
